Basic Information for CVE-2026-44496 Vulnerability Information Axios: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) via Cookie Name Injection Overview When handling CSRF protection, Axios directly uses unescaped configuration items (the XSRF cookie name) to construct a regular expression. Affected Versions Axios 0.x series: versions below 0.32.0 Axios 1.x series: versions below 1.16.0 Details Vulnerability Principle: When constructing the regular expression used to match the XSRF cookie, Axios fails to escape regex metacharacters present in cookie names that are user-configurable or controllable by the user. Trigger Conditions: The attacker must be able to influence the cookie name configuration passed to Axios. Execution Environment: The vulnerability is effective only in the standard browser environment where document.cookie is read. Unaffected Environments: The Node.js HTTP adapter, React Native, and Web Workers are not affected, as Axios does not read document.cookie in these environments. Impact Client-side Availability Degradation: Primarily causes browser tabs to freeze or become unresponsive. Denial of Service (DoS): Consumes significant computational resources to handle regex backtracking, leading to severe performance degradation on the client-side frontend and impacting normal interactions. Technical details The root cause is in lib/helpers/cookies.js at line 33, where the read(name) function constructs a RegExp object by directly concatenating the unsanitized name parameter: document.cookie.match(new RegExp('(?:^|; )' + name + '=([^;])')). Because regex metacharacters in name are not escaped, an attacker who can influence the xsrfCookieName configuration — via prototype pollution, configuration injection, or direct calls to the internal cookie helper — can inject patterns such as (.+)+$ that trigger catastrophic backtracking (CWE-1333, CWE-400). The xsrfCookieName value flows from Axios configuration through lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js (1.x) or lib/adapters/xhr.js (0.x) into the vulnerable cookies.read() call. The fix replaces dynamic regex construction with a string-splitting approach that compares cookie names using exact string equality (GitHub Advisory). Impact Exploitation causes client-side availability degradation: a crafted cookie name of approximately 20–30 characters can freeze the affected browser tab for seconds to minutes, blocking all UI interaction and JavaScript execution due to JavaScript's single-threaded event loop. In Server-Side Rendering (SSR) frameworks where this code path is exercised, the Node.js event loop can be stalled, rendering the server unresponsive to all requests. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact — credentials are not exposed and requests are not modified (GitHub Advisory). Exploitability A proof-of-concept demonstrating the ReDoS behavior is publicly available in the official security advisory, showing exponential timing growth (e.g., ~21ms at input length 20, ~1,344ms at length 26, extrapolated to ~5+ minutes at length 30). However, the PoC only simulates local browser behavior and does not constitute a weaponized exploit targeting real deployments.
